claims.text: The proposed intervention is to develop a computational model that predicts how local chemical order affects mechanical properties in high-entropy alloys.
Local chemical order affects the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
Predicting the effects of local chemical order will enable researchers to design and optimize new high-entropy alloys.
Model-guided alloy design will produce improved combinations of strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance.
The expected property combination will improve relative to the current state of the art in high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis is intended to apply under operating conditions relevant to structural applications.
The model is limited to predicting effects associated with local chemical order.
Factors other than local chemical order can affect the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
The model's predictive accuracy is uncertain.
The model's predictive accuracy will depend on the quality of its input data.
The model's predictive accuracy will depend on the complexity of relationships among microstructure, local chemical order, and mechanical properties.
A model-designed alloy can be evaluated by experimentally measuring its strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance.
Failure of the measured properties to match the model predictions would falsify the hypothesis.
